newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends rise on cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power extends rise on cold.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. extended Monday's rise ahead of a cold snap forecast to hit the region Wednesday.
"Everyone is trying to line up their delivery schedule," said a marketer in Houston.
Wednesday after scattered rain showers and flurries today, temperatures at the midsection of the Atlantic seaboard were predicted to peak in 30s F and bottom in the 20s.
Low temperatures, running 10-15 degrees below the seasonal average, were forecast to last until the weekend.

Firm, peak electricity scheduled in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district for Wednesday was pegged at $25.25-$26.25 a megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching Monday's high of $27.00 in early trading.
The latest quote, following deals done mostly in the $25.50-$26.25 range, compared with Monday's $24.00-$25.00.
Firm, peak PJM power for Thursday was talked near $24.00 and for Friday $24.75.
Firm, off-peak PJM electricity for Wednesday was assessed near $17.25, Thursday $16.00 and Friday $17.00, compared with Monday's $18.00.
A rebound in Gulf Coast natural gas prices helped boost PJM physical prices, brokers and marketers said.
NYMEX January 1997 Henry Hub natural gas futures climbed 6.1 cents per million British thermal units to $3.555 after hitting an intraday high of $3.600.
December PJM power was valued at $28.75-$28.95, up from Monday's $28.65-$26.85.
January/February 1997 PJM electricity was assessed at $33.35-$33.65, up slightly from Monday's $33.15-$33.60.
March 1997 PJM deliveries were thinly talked in the $25.50-$26.40 range, compared with a quote of $24.90-$25.15 Monday.
Second-quarter 1997 PJM deliveries were discussed at $22.75-$22.90, compared with a Monday deal reported near $22.85.
July/August 1997 PJM power was quoted near $32.05, compared with Monday's range $31.75-$32.00.
Brokers and marketers expect PJM activity would slow considerably by midday Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday weekend in the U.S., which begins Thursday.
